title: Which physicians do we turn people from?
source_text: Ἐπεὶ δὲ καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα παραπλήσιόν φησι ποιεῖν τὸν τὰ χριστιανισμοῦ διδάσκοντα τῷ ὑπισχνουμένῳ μὲν ὑγιῆ ποιεῖν τὰ σώματα, ἀποτρέποντι δὲ τοῦ προσέχειν τοῖς ἐπιστήμοσιν ἰατροῖς τῷ ἐλέγχεσθαι ὑπ᾿ αὐτῶν τὴν ἰδιωτείαν αὐτοῦ, καὶ πρὸς ταῦτα ἐροῦμεν· τίνας φῂς ἰατροὺς, ἀφ᾿ ὧν ἀποτρέπομεν τοὺς ἰδιώτας; οὐ γὰρ δὴ ὑπολαμβάνεις τοῖς φιλοσοφοῦσι προσάγειν ἡμᾶς τὴν εἰς τὸν λόγον προτροπὴν, ἵν᾿ ἐκείνους νομίσῃς εἶναι ἰατροὺς, ἀφ᾿ ὧν ἀποτρέπομεν οὓς ἐπὶ τὸν θεῖον καλοῦμεν λόγον. ἤτοι οὖν οὐκ ἀποκρίνεται μὴ ἔχων λέγειν τοὺς ἰατροὺς. ἢ ἀνάγκη αὐτὸν καταφεύγειν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἰδιώτας, οἳ καὶ αὐτοὶ περιηχοῦσιν ἀνδραποδωδῶς τὰ περὶ πολλῶν θεῶν καὶ ὅσα ἄλλα λέγοιεν ἂν ἰδιῶται. ἑκατέρως οὖν ἐλεγχθήσεται μάτην παραλαβὼν ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τὸν ἀποτρέποντα τῶν ἐπιστημόνων ἰατρῶν. ἵνα δὲ καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἐπικούρου φιλοσοφίας καὶ τῶν κατ᾿ Ἐπίκουρον νομιζομένων Ἐπικουρείων ἰατρῶν ἀποτρέπωμεν τοὺς ἐν ἐκείνοις ἀπατωμένους, πῶς οὐχὶ εὐλογώτατα ποιήσομεν ἀφιστάντες νόσου χαλεπῆς, ἣν ἐνεποίησαν οἱ Κέλσου ἰατροὶ. τῆς κατὰ τὴν ἀναίρεσιν τῆς προνοίας καὶ εἰσαγωγὴν τῆς ἡδονῆς ὡς ἀγαθοῦ; ἀλλ᾿ ἔστω ἰατρῶν ἡμᾶς ἄλλων φιλοσόφων ἀφιστάνειν τούτους, οὓς προτρέπομεν ἐπὶ τὸν ἡμέτερον λόγον. τῶν ἀπὸ τοῦ Περιπάτου. ἀναιρούντων τὴν πρὸς ἡμᾶς πρόνοιαν καὶ τὴν σχέσιν πρὸς ἀνθρώπους τοῦ θείου· πῶς οὐχὶ εὐσεβεῖς μὲν ἡμεῖς κατασκευάσομεν καὶ θεραπεύσομεν τοὺς προτετραμμένους, πείθοντες αὐτοὺς ἀνακεῖσθαι τῷ ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεῷ, μεγάλων δὲ τραυμάτων, τῶν ἀπὸ λόγων νομιζομένων φιλοσόφων, ἀπαλλάσσομεν τοὺς πειθομένους ἡμῖν; ἀλλὰ καὶ ἄλλους δεδόσθω ἡμᾶς ἀποτρέπειν ἀπὸ ἰατρῶν Στωϊκῶν θεὸν φθαρτὸν εἰσαγόντων καὶ τὴν οὐσίαν αὐτοῦ λεγόντων σῶμα τρεπτὸν δι᾿ ὅλων καὶ ἀλλοιωτὸν καὶ μεταβλητὸν. καί ποτε πάντα φθειρόντων καὶ μόνον τὸν θεὸν καταλειπόντων· πῶς οὐχὶ καὶ οὕτως κακῶν μὲν ἀπαλλάξομεν τοὺς πειθομένους. προσάξομεν δ᾿ εὐσεβεῖ λόγῳ τῷ περὶ τοῦ ἀνακεῖσθαι τῷ δημιουργῷ καὶ θαυμάζειν τὸν πατέρα τῆς Χριστιανῶν διδασκαλίας. φιλανθρωπότατα ἐπιστρεπτικὸν καὶ ψυχῶν μαθήματα οἰκονομήσαντα ἐπισπαρῆναι ὅλῳ τῷ τῶν ἀνθρώπων γένει; ἀλλὰ κἂν τοὺς πεπονθότας τὴν περὶ μετενσωματώσεως ἄνοιαν ἀπὸ ἰατρῶν, τῶν καταβιβαζόντων τὴν λογικὴν φύσιν ὁτὲ μὲν ἐπὶ τὴν ἄλογον πᾶσαν ὁτὲ δὲ καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν ἀφάνταστον. θεραπεύωμεν· πῶς οὐ βελτίονας ταῖς ψυχαῖς κατασκευάσομεν τοὺς πειθομένους λόγῳ. οὐ διδάσκοντι μὲν ἐν κολάσεως μοίρᾳ τῷ φαύλῳ ἀποδίδοσθαι ἀναισθησίαν ἢ ἀλογίαν, παριστάντι δὲ εἶναί τινα φάρμακα ἐπιστρεπτικὰ τοὺς ἀπὸ θεοῦ τοῖς φαύλοις προσαγομένους πόνους καὶ τὰς κολάσεις; τοῦτο γὰρ οἱ φρονίμως Χριστιανοὶ ζῶντες φρονοῦντες οἰκονομοῦσι τοὺς ἁπλουστέρους. ὡς καὶ οἱ πατέρες τοὺς κομιδῇ νηπίους. οὐ γὰρ καταφεύγομεν οὖν ἐπὶ νηπίους καὶ ἠλιθίους ἀγροίκους λέγοντες αὐτοῖς· φεύγετε τοὺς ἰατροὺς. οὐδὲ λέγομεν· ὁρᾶτε μή ποτε τὶς ὑμῶν ἐπιστήμης ἐπιλάβηται. οὐδὲ φάσκομεν ὅτι κακόν ἐστιν ἐπιστήμη, οὐδὲ μεμήναμεν, ἵν᾿ εἴπωμεν ὅτι γνῶσις σφάλλει τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἀπὸ τῆς κατὰ ψυχὴν ὑγείας. ἀλλ᾿ οὐδ᾿ ἀπόλλυσθαι ἀπὸ σοφίας εἴποιμεν ἄν τινα πώποτε, οἵτινες οὐδὲ τὸ ἐμοὶ προσέχετε. κἂν διδάσκωμεν. φαμὲν. ἀλλά· τῷ θεῷ τῶν ὅλων προσέχετε καὶ διδασκάλῳ τῶν περὶ αὐτοῦ μαθημάτων τῷ Ἰησοῦ. οὐδεὶς δ᾿ ἡμῶν οὕτως ἐστὶν ἀλαζὼν, ἵν᾿ ὅπερ Κέλσος περιέθηκε τῷ τοῦ διδάσκοντος προσώπῳ εἴποι πρὸς τοὺς γνωρίμους. τὸ ἐγὼ ὑμᾶς σώσω μόνος. ὅρα οὖν. πόσα ἡμῶν καταψεύδεται. ἀλλ᾿ οὐδέ φαμεν ὅτι οἱ ἀληθῶς ἰατροὶ φθείρουσιν ους ἐπαγγέλλονται θεραπεύειν.
pass_a_gloss: Since also after these things he says (φησι) that the one teaching (διδάσκων) the things of Christianity (χριστιανισμός) does something like (παραπλήσιον) one promising (ὑπισχνέομαι) to make bodies healthy (ὑγιής) but turning away (ἀποτρέπω) from attending (προσέχω) to the skilled (ἐπιστήμων) physicians (ἰατρός), because his own lack of skill (ἰδιωτεία) is exposed (ἐλέγχω) by them, to these too we shall say: which physicians do you mean, from whom we turn away the unlearned (ἰδιῶται)? For surely you do not suppose that to those philosophising (φιλοσοφέω) we bring the exhortation (προτροπή) to the word (λόγος), so that you consider them the physicians from whom we turn away those whom we call (καλέω) to the divine word. Either then he does not answer, having none to name, or he must take refuge (καταφεύγω) in the unlearned, who themselves echo about (περιηχέω) slavishly (ἀνδραποδωδῶς) the things about many gods and whatever else unlearned would say. Either way he will be refuted, having vainly (μάτην) brought into the argument the one turning away from skilled physicians. But if from the philosophy of Epicurus and from those considered Epicurean physicians according to Epicurus we turn away those deceived (ἀπατάω) among them, how shall we not act most reasonably (εὐλογώτατα), withdrawing (ἀφίστημι) them from a grievous disease (νόσος χαλεπή) which Celsus's physicians produced in them, that consisting in the abolition (ἀναίρεσις) of providence (πρόνοια) and introduction (εἰσαγωγή) of pleasure (ἡδονή) as good? But let it be that we withdraw from other physicians, philosophers, those whom we exhort to our word, those from the Peripatos, abolishing providence toward us and the relation (σχέσις) of the divine (τὸ θεῖον) toward humans: how shall we not make pious (εὐσεβής) and heal (θεραπεύω) those converted (προτρέπω), persuading them to be devoted (ἀνακεῖσθαι) to the God over all, and free (ἀπαλλάσσω) from great wounds (τραῦμα), those from arguments of so-called philosophers, those obeying us? But let it be granted that we turn others away from Stoic physicians, introducing a perishable (φθαρτός) God and saying his substance (οὐσία) is body changeable throughout (τρεπτὸν δι᾿ ὅλων), alterable (ἀλλοιωτός), mutable (μεταβλητός), and at some time destroying all things and leaving God alone: how shall we not thus too free from evils those obeying, and bring them to the pious doctrine (εὐσεβὴς λόγος) of being devoted to the Creator (δημιουργός) and admiring (θαυμάζω) the father [= author] of the Christians' teaching (διδασκαλία), who most lovingly toward mankind (φιλανθρωπότατα) arranged (οἰκονομέω) converting (ἐπιστρεπτικός) lessons (μαθήματα) of souls to be sown over (ἐπισπείρω) the whole race of humans? And if we heal those who have suffered the folly (ἄνοια) about transmigration (μετενσωμάτωσις) from physicians bringing down (καταβιβάζω) the rational nature (λογικὴ φύσις) sometimes to the wholly irrational (ἄλογος), sometimes even to the unimagining (ἀφάνταστος), how shall we not make better in souls those obeying a doctrine not teaching that insensibility (ἀναισθησία) or irrationality (ἀλογία) is given to the wicked (φαῦλος) as a portion (μοῖρα) of punishment (κόλασις), but presenting the pains (πόνοι) and punishments brought by God on the wicked as certain converting remedies (φάρμακα ἐπιστρεπτικά)? For this thinking, Christians living wisely (φρονίμως) manage (οἰκονομέω) the simpler (ἁπλούστεροι), as fathers the very young (νήπιοι). We do not take refuge in children and stupid rustics (ἠλίθιοι ἄγροικοι), saying to them: flee the physicians; nor say: see that none of you lays hold of knowledge (ἐπιστήμη); nor assert knowledge is evil (κακόν); nor are we mad (μεμήναμεν), to say knowledge (γνῶσις) trips (σφάλλω) men from health (ὑγεία) of soul. Nor would we ever say anyone perishes (ἀπόλλυμαι) from wisdom (σοφία), we who do not say even when teaching: attend to me, but: attend to the God of the universe and to the teacher of the lessons about him, Jesus. None of us is so boastful (ἀλαζών) as to say what Celsus put on (περιτίθημι) the character (πρόσωπον) of the teacher to his pupils (γνώριμοι): I alone will save (σῴζω) you. See then how much he lies against (καταψεύδομαι) us. Nor do we say the true physicians destroy (φθείρω) those they profess to heal.
pass_b_english: After this he says that the man who teaches the things of Christianity acts much like one who promises to make bodies well, yet turns people away from heeding skilled physicians, because they would expose his own lack of skill. To this too we shall reply: Which physicians do you mean, from whom we turn away the unlearned? For you surely do not suppose that we bring our call to the word to people who study philosophy, so that you might take them to be the physicians from whom we turn away those we summon to the divine word. Either, then, he gives no answer, since he cannot name the physicians, or he must fall back on the unlearned, who themselves go about repeating like slaves what is said of many gods and whatever else the unlearned might say. Either way he will be shown to have brought into his argument, to no purpose, the man who turns people away from skilled physicians.

And even supposing that we turn away from the philosophy of Epicurus, and from the physicians reckoned Epicureans after Epicurus, those who have been deceived by them, how shall we not be acting with the best of reason when we draw them away from a grievous disease which the physicians of Celsus have put into them, the disease of doing away with providence and bringing in pleasure as a good? Or let it be granted that we draw those whom we urge toward our word away from other physicians, philosophers of the Peripatetic school, who do away with providence toward us and with the relation of the divine to human beings. How shall we not make those we have converted godly, and heal them, by persuading them to devote themselves to the God who is over all, and free those who listen to us from great wounds, the wounds that come from the arguments of so-called philosophers?

Let it be granted too that we turn others away from Stoic physicians, who bring in a God who can perish and say that His substance is a body that can be changed throughout, altered and transformed, and who at some time destroy all things and leave God alone. How shall we not, in this case also, free from evils those who listen to us, and bring them to the godly doctrine that teaches them to devote themselves to the Creator and to marvel at the father of the Christian teaching, who out of the greatest love for mankind arranged for teachings that turn souls back to be sown throughout the whole human race? And if we heal those who have caught the folly of transmigration from physicians who bring the rational nature down, sometimes into any irrational nature at all, and sometimes even into a nature without sense-impressions, how shall we not make better in soul those who listen to a doctrine that does not teach that the wicked man is given insensibility or irrationality as his share of punishment, but shows that the pains and punishments God brings on the wicked are remedies meant to turn them back? For Christians who live wisely guide the simpler ones with this in mind, as fathers guide their very little children.

We do not, then, turn to children and foolish rustics and say to them, “Flee the physicians.” Nor do we say, “Take care that none of you ever lays hold of knowledge.” Nor do we assert that knowledge is an evil, nor are we so mad as to say that knowledge leads people astray from health of soul. Nor would we ever say that anyone perishes from wisdom, we who do not say even when we teach, “Attend to me,” but, “Attend to the God of the universe, and to Jesus, the teacher of the lessons about Him.” None of us is such a braggart as to say to his disciples what Celsus put into the mouth of the teacher: “I alone will save you.” See, then, how many lies he tells about us. Nor do we say that the true physicians destroy those they promise to heal.

choices.choice: Copy-text: staged source_3.json section 75 (Koetschau 3.75). Several staged stops (e.g. 'ἐπὶ τὸν θεῖον καλοῦμεν λόγον. ἤτοι', 'τῶν ἀπὸ τοῦ Περιπάτου.', 'κἂν διδάσκωμεν. φαμὲν.') are punctuation noise from the TEI and were read through as one sentence. 'ἐπιστρεπτικὸν καὶ ψυχῶν μαθήματα' is grammatically odd (singular ἐπιστρεπτικόν beside plural μαθήματα; a word may have dropped out, e.g. 'converting and saving lessons for souls'); rendered as 'teachings that turn souls back' — doubtful reading. 'ἀφάνταστον' (a nature without impressions/imagination) means plant life in the transmigration theory; kept as 'a nature without sense-impressions' rather than naming plants. 'τὸν πατέρα τῆς Χριστιανῶν διδασκαλίας' uses the Platonic idiom 'father of a discourse' (its author or originator); reviewer set it lowercase ('the father of the Christian teaching') so the English does not decide between God and Christ as the referent, which the Greek leaves open (paired with 'the Creator', God is the likelier reading). The quoted phrases 'Flee the physicians', 'Take care that none of you ever lays hold of knowledge', knowledge as evil, knowledge leading astray from health of soul, perishing from wisdom, and 'I alone will save you' all echo Celsus's caricature of the Christian teacher; put in double quotation marks only where Origen gives them as direct speech. No Scripture quotation or clear allusion in this chapter.

Restored the structure of 'ἀπὸ τῆς Ἐπικούρου φιλοσοφίας ... ἀποτρέπωμεν τοὺς ... ἀπατωμένους': the English had dropped 'turn away from' the Epicurean philosophy and physicians and made them only the source of deception; now 'turn away from the philosophy of Epicurus, and from the physicians ..., those who have been deceived by them', with 'ἵνα δὲ καί' as 'even supposing'

'the Father of the Christian teaching' set lowercase as 'the father of the Christian teaching' (Platonic idiom 'father of a discourse' = its author); the capital forced God the Father where the Greek leaves God or Christ open; pronoun 'His' removed by recasting 'φιλανθρωπότατα' as 'out of the greatest love for mankind'
'into the wholly irrational' changed to 'into any irrational nature at all' (ἐπὶ τὴν ἄλογον πᾶσαν means every irrational kind, not a degree of irrationality)
'take refuge with children' changed to 'turn to children' (καταφεύγομεν ἐπί = resort to; avoids a calque)
Checked: no Scripture citation needed; Celsus's caricatured sayings stay in quotation marks as direct speech; 'the God who is over all', 'Creator', capitals for God correct
